summary: Suzuki's first battery-electric car in Australia is a 4.28m small SUV built in India on a BYD-supplied LFP battery, sold in Victoria as the 49kWh front-drive Motion and the 61kWh dual-motor Ultra. Reviewers broadly agree it drives well and feels a class above its price inside, and broadly agree it is priced above what its 344-395km WLTP range and 70kW DC charging justify against BYD, MG and Kia rivals. Suzuki advertises drive-away prices only; the $47,990 and $56,990 used here are the manufacturer RRPs implied by Suzuki's own '10% off RRP' offer and matched by Glass's MSRP, and Suzuki's advertised drive-away offers ($46,990 and $56,990 in November 2026) sit below what those RRPs plus Victorian on-roads would cost.
pros: Five years/unlimited kilometres of warranty with no servicing conditions attached — Suzuki Australia advertises no longer conditional term, unlike MG, Nissan or Hyundai, so the headline number is the number you actually get; the traction battery is separately covered for 8 years/160,000km.
The Ultra's ALLGRIP-e dual-motor all-wheel drive makes 135kW/307Nm and runs 0-100km/h in 7.4 seconds; the BYD Atto 2, MG S5 EV and Kia EV3 rivals it is cross-shopped against are front-drive only.

The rear bench slides and reclines, so boot space moves between 244 litres with maximum rear legroom and 310 litres with the bench forward in the Motion (238-306 litres in the Ultra), and up to 562 litres with the seats folded — you choose legroom or luggage per trip.

Capped-price servicing is covered by Suzuki's 5-year/100,000km Genuine Service Program at 12-month/20,000km intervals, and a Type 2 AC charging cable Suzuki values at over $1,000 is standard on both grades.
Suzuki has one of the larger established dealer and parts networks in regional Australia, which is a real difference from the newer Chinese brands the e Vitara is priced against.
cons: At $47,990 and $56,990 RRP (Suzuki advertises $46,990 and $56,990 drive-away), it costs well over $10,000 more than a BYD Atto 2 and more than the MG S5 EV and Kia EV3, yet the Motion's 344km WLTP only matches the cheaper Atto 2 and MG S5 49kWh and falls well short of the EV3's 436-604km — CarExpert and EV Central both make price the central criticism.
CarsGuide measured about 295km in the Ultra against its 395km WLTP claim, a shortfall near 100km, and recorded 17.9kWh/100km against the 16.5kWh/100km official figure.
DC charging peaks around 70kW for a 45-minute 10-80% stop on both battery sizes — slow for 2026 — and there is no vehicle-to-load outlet.
Four stars from ANCAP in 2026, with 77% adult occupant protection and no head-protecting centre airbag; most direct rivals hold five stars.

Victorian buyers get two grades only. The 61kWh front-drive Ultra — the longest-range e Vitara, listed at $51,990 MSRP — is sold solely by the separate Suzuki Queensland distributor covering Queensland and the Northern Rivers of NSW, and cannot be ordered here.
